papers.title_in_file: Quantum Natural Language Processing: A Comprehensive Review of Models, Methods, and Applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 6.2 to 6.4 and Conclusion; the survey tables and reference list were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum natural language processing models, encodings and optimisation methods.

assertions.value: The authors state that QNLP approaches are still limited, mainly used on small datasets, with only a few models explored extensively.
quotes: It is emphasised that QNLP approaches are still limited, mainly used on small datasets, with only a few models (like QCM and HCM) explored extensively, indicating the need for further research to scale quantum NLP methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own survey finding; an observation about the literature they reviewed.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum circuit models, covering variational quantum circuits and quantum neural networks, are the most extensively utilised QNLP framework across the NLP tasks they surveyed.
quotes: Quantum circuit models, encompassing variational quantum circuits and quantum neural networks, represent the most extensively utilised QNLP framework across a variety of NLP tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Count-based survey observation from one review.

assertions.value: The authors propose six general categories of QNLP models, based on the quantum computing principles used and the computational approach.
quotes: six general categories of QNLP models are categorised as:
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own classification proposal.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum encoding techniques offer quantum speedups, better accuracy and improved security.
quotes: offering quantum speedups, better accuracy, and improved security.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the conclusion without evidence given in the paper's own results.
assertions.reader_inference: The survey does not test this; treat as an author claim.

papers.title_in_file: Complex-Phase Extensions of Szegedy Quantum Walk on Graphs
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section III to VI headings and Conclusions; the proofs and Section VII algorithm details were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper extending Szegedy quantum walks with link phases and local arbitrary phase rotations.

assertions.value: The authors state that their classical simulation algorithm for the graph-phased Szegedy quantum walk scales as O(N 2) in both time and memory, against previous algorithms scaling as O(N 3).
quotes: This algorithm scales as O(N 2) in both time and memory requirements, so that is more efficient than previous algorithms scaling as O(N 3).
assertions.certainty_reason: Complexity statement of the authors' own algorithm; no formal theorem was located in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that marking nodes with a null local APR phase is equivalent to marking with absorbing vertices when the double Szegedy operator Ws is used.
quotes: We have shown that marking with a null local APR phase is totally equivalent to marking with absorbing vertices in the case of using the double Szegedy operator Ws.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own derivation (Section VI); not read through in full.

assertions.value: The authors state that when all phase values differ the circuits would be inefficient, and that an efficient implementation is possible when the phases follow symmetric patterns.
quotes: In general cases where all the phase values would be different, the circuits would be inefficient.
the phases can be distributed in some symmetric patterns so that an efficient implementation is possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusions p.17 state the limit on circuit efficiency in the paper's own words.

papers.title_in_file: Physics-Informed Quantum Machine Learning: Solving nonlinear differential equations in latent spaces without costly grid evaluations
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, simulation section and Conclusion; the encoding derivations and appendices were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal for a physics-informed quantum algorithm that solves differential equations in a latent space of state overlaps.

assertions.value: The authors propose a physics-informed quantum algorithm for nonlinear and multidimensional differential equations in a quantum latent space, with a loss built from state overlaps that does not require independent sequential function evaluations on grid points.
quotes: We propose a physics-informed quantum algorithm to solve nonlinear and multidimensional differential equations (DEs) in a quantum latent space.
we construct a loss that does not require independent sequential function evaluations on grid points.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposal stated in the abstract; supported only by statevector simulation in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that for some bases, encoding nonlinearity requires only an additive linear increase of the system size, O(N + p), in the degree of nonlinearity p.
quotes: for some bases requiring only an additive linear increase of the system size O(N + p) in the degree of nonlinearity p.
assertions.certainty_reason: Scaling stated by the authors for their encoding; no theorem was located in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors report that they tested the algorithm by full statevector simulation in Julia with Yao.jl, using the Chebyshev encoding with four qubits.
quotes: We use the Julia programming language and the Yao.jl package [113] for the full statevector simulation.
In particular we use the Chebyshev encoding and represent the function using four qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup in the simulation section.
assertions.reader_inference: Only statevector simulation at small qubit count is reported, so no hardware result is shown.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms for Molecular Docking
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Methods overview, Results and Discussion and Conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A Pfizer and Nvidia study applying digitized counterdiabatic QAOA to molecular docking, cast as a max-clique problem, in GPU simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulated quantum runs were conducted on a GPU cluster and that they examined 14 and 17 nodes instances.
quotes: Simulated quantum runs were conducted on a GPU cluster.
We examined 14 and 17 nodes instances
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own setup: simulated runs, not quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that for their 14-qubit instance the most sampled bitstring corresponds to the actual ground-truth state, and that warm-starting left the convergence time approximately the same.
quotes: Results on 14-qubits The computational results for the 14-qubit instance were obtained using the COBYQA algorithm.
The most sampled bitstring correspond to the actual ground-truth state.
However, for this specific instance the convergence time remains approximately the same.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-instance empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the penalty increased to 2 and the number of layers equal to 1, all three methods (cold start, linear warm start and quadratic warm start) gave no solution.
quotes: In the last case, increasing the penalty to 2 and having number of layers equal to 1, all three methods are not giving any solution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study empirical result.

papers.title_in_file: On quantum factoring using noisy intermediate scale quantum computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 2 start and Section 9 Conclusions; mid-sections on resource estimates and numerical tables were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of the variational quantum factoring algorithm comparing VQE and QAOA optimisers, resource costs and entanglement.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQE consistently achieves lower energies than QAOA for their factoring instances.
quotes: We compared two quantum algorithms for ground state finding in VQF and found that VQE consistently achieves lower energies than QAOA for our factoring instances.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on its own instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that the time required for quantum circuit gradient evaluation overwhelms the time required for complete classical factoring, for the range of m they studied.
quotes: Therefore the time required for quantum circuit gradient evaluation overwhelms the time required for complete classical factoring for the range of m we studied.
assertions.certainty_reason: Resource estimate from one study over a limited range of m.

assertions.value: The authors report that the entangled circuit found similar final energies as the unentangled circuit on average for m = 91.
quotes: We found that the entangled circuit found similar final energies as the unentangled circuit on average for m = 91.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-instance simulation result.

papers.title_in_file: Use VQE to calculate the ground energy of hydrogen molecules on IBM Quantum
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section V Summary; the theory background and circuit code were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial-style study computing the hydrogen molecule ground-state energy with VQE in Qiskit on the IBM Quantum platform.

assertions.value: The authors state that they implement VQE using Qiskit on the IBM Quantum platform to calculate the ground state energy of a hydrogen molecule.
quotes: we introduce quantum computing and implement the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithm using Qiskit on the IBM Quantum platform to calculate the ground state energy of a hydrogen molecule.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that at distance 0.725 the VQE energy was −1.134167 against an actual −1.117506, an error of about 1.47%, and that the difference 0.016661 exceeds the chemical precision 0.0016.
quotes: that is, dist = 0.725, the actual data Hh = −1.117506, and the data obtained by our VQE algorithm is Hh = −1.134167, the error is about 1.47%
Although the data difference 0.016661 is greater than the chemical precision 0.0016, it is still a relatively accurate solution method.
assertions.certainty_reason: One small molecule, one study; the summary does not say clearly whether this figure came from simulation or hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that on an actual quantum device there is a large background noise, owing to current device limitations, which will affect the coherence and so the result.
quotes: Especially when running an algorithm on an actual quantum device, due to the limitations of the current quantum device, there is a large background noise, which will affect the coherence of the quantum, thereby affecting the result.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of a limitation without a measurement in the text read.

papers.title_in_file: Deep Quantum Neural Networks are Gaussian Process
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Figure 2 caption and Conclusion; the derivations and appendices were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper arguing that overparameterized, deep variational quantum circuits behave as a Gaussian process, with finite-width corrections.

assertions.value: The authors state that initializing parameters from a random Haar distribution results in the QNN behaving similarly to a Gaussian Process at wide width or, empirically, at deep depth.
quotes: We observe the influence of initializing parameters using random Haar distribution results in the QNN behaving similarly to a Gaussian Process (QNN-GP) at wide width or, empirically, at a deep depth.
We obsereved theortically and by simulation that this led to a shift in the output distribution of the quantum models towards a Gaussian process.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation plus simulation; no theorem statement with stated conditions was located in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors present a framework that examines the impact of finite width in a closed-form relationship using a 1/d expansion, where d represents the dimension of the circuit's Hilbert space.
quotes: Moreover, we present a framework to examine the impact of finite width in the closed-form relationship using a 1/d expansion, where d represents the dimension of the circuit's Hilbert space.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own framework statement.

assertions.value: The authors report simulations of circuits built from random two-qubit gates with MNIST input reduced by PCA, and observe that as the QNN becomes deeper the output distribution tends to converge more towards a Gaussian distribution.
quotes: Each layer of the circuit consists of random two-qubit gates followed by entanglement gates.
The input of the circuit was constructed from the MNIST dataset, reduced size with the Principal Component Analysis(PAC)
As observed, as the quantum neural network (QNN) becomes deeper, the output distribution tends to converge more towards a Gaussian distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation illustration in one figure.

papers.title_in_file: Continuous-Variable Quantum Encoding Techniques: A Comparative Study of Embedding Techniques and Their Impact on Machine Learning Performance
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, dataset and Methods paragraphs and Conclusion; per-model result tables were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical comparison of continuous-variable and IQP quantum encodings feeding classical models on a telecom churn dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that IQP encoding consistently underperforms, while Displacement and Squeezing encodings demonstrate notable improvements.
quotes: However, the choice of encoding plays a crucial role, as IQP encoding consistently underperforms, while Displacement and Squeezing encodings demonstrate notable improvements.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one dataset in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that PCA dimensionality reduction consistently improves model performance, with PCA=23 yielding the highest accuracy across most scenarios.
quotes: PCA dimensionality reduction consistently improves model performance, with PCA=23 yielding the highest accuracy across most scenarios.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one dataset in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they implemented the machine learning algorithms using the PennyLane library for a customer churn classification problem in the telecommunications domain.
quotes: We implemented a set of machine learning algorithms using the PennyLane open-source software library to address a customer churn classification problem within the telecommunications domain.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup and the single dataset domain it tests.
assertions.reader_inference: One telecom churn dataset, run on a simulator.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum encoding techniques introduce computational overhead, particularly in high-dimensional feature spaces.
quotes: Despite their potential, quantum encoding techniques introduce computational overhead, particularly in high-dimensional feature spaces.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated cost of the encodings from their experiments.
